## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāketajātaka* (Ja 237) is a birth story in the *Dukanipāta* of the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1879]. Framed by the opening verse question *Ko nu kho bhagavā hetu* ("Why are hearts cold..."), the story was delivered by the Buddha while residing near the city of Sāketa, concerning an elderly brahmin of Sāketa [Fausböll 1879; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. The prose commentary explicitly observes that both the background story of the present (*paccuppannavatthu*) and the narrative of the past (*atītavatthu*) are identical to those previously related in the First Book (*Ekanipāta*, Ja 68) [Fausböll 1879]. In the resolution (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains that the elderly brahmin and his wife had been his parents in former lives, and he himself was their son [Fausböll 1879].

 According to automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits internal Pali textual reuse with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, centered on segments §2.1–2.4 (each sharing over 300 characters at 0.93 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels meeting the match threshold are reported by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
